commits.message: feat(cli): legion threads resolve resolves the review threads the reviewer accepted
docs(legion): who resolves review threads and why the review App cannot

deviations: `--repo <owner>/<name>` is a required flag (nothing in a pane's environment names the repository; the daemon's state response carries none and adding one is a daemon-API bump). Accepted by the architect before implementation.
`skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md` gains one paragraph after the sign-off order: the action ask for a thread GitHub refuses to resolve. Accepted by the architect before implementation.
trickyParts: cmdGh's grant redemption is extracted verbatim into `redeemGitHubToken` (same request body, same error strings, same child env); `legion gh`'s 22 existing tests are the regression lock. PR #992 (LEGION-54) rewrites `grantFrom` and cmdGh's spawn line; if it lands first and GitHub reports CONFLICTING, the plan's step-1 note records the cmdGh resolution.

GraphQL Bot logins are the bare App slug (`legion-implementer`), never `<slug>[bot]`; the acceptance rule compares the opener's and newest comment's logins from the same query, never against `/gh-token`'s `appLogin`.

The bash tool prepends the real `LEGION_GRANT` to every command; a second, imitated `export LEGION_GRANT=` line in the command text shadows it and every `legion …`/credential-helper call answers 403 (`could not read Username` from `jj git push`). Running grant-needing commands through the eval kernel's `tool.bash` bridge, with the shell command in a script file, kept the command text clean.

The shared jj op log (one repo, ~25 issue workspaces) raced my `git push` with another workspace's op; the automatic reconcile re-minted this workspace's working-copy commit as an empty one and hid the old one whose only content was the 0-byte, extension-provisioned `.omp/config.yml`. `jj workspace update-stale` with that file backed up and restored recovered it; nothing tracked was lost.
No `pr-checks-result` job exists in this repository's workflows; the PR body's CI line cites the `Tests` workflow run (34741048302) at the head instead.
